title: Completing a set becomes an explicit domain operation
context: set.win and game.win are written in exactly one place: processGamePhase inside the frontend rally helper, which the server reached only because it overwrote the whole document. Once a rally write is a plain append, neither field is ever written again. The recording page does not break, because isSetInProgress is derived from entries in the Redux initialize reducer, but findGameSummaries reads $$set.win to count sets won and projects game.win, so the game list would show zero sets won and a result frozen at the value create-game writes on creation. Nothing would report an error. The root cause is that finishing a set is currently a side effect of recording a rally rather than an operation in its own right.
decision: Add a completeSet domain operation. After appending an entry the use case derives whether the set has finished and, when it has, writes sets.N.win with a positional set, together with game.win when the match result is decided. This happens at most once per set rather than once per rally, so it is not the per-rally accumulation this Change removes; it is a derived value written at a defined point with a consumer that requires it. Alongside it, the initial value of a game's win becomes null rather than false, and GameSummary.win widens to boolean or null, so that undecided is representable rather than indistinguishable from a loss.

alternatives.option: Derive win everywhere and store nothing
alternatives.reason: The game summary aggregation would have to compare the last rally's scores and apply the scoring rules inside the pipeline, giving the volleyball rules a second implementation in the hardest place to test.

alternatives.option: Let the client declare in the request that the set has finished
alternatives.reason: It puts the trust boundary on the wrong side and contradicts the server-authoritative scoring that synchronised recording requires.

consequences: The server judges set completion, which requires the set-phase rule in the domain layer and is the first step toward server-authoritative scoring.
The game summary aggregation and the game list keep working unchanged.
A new game reads as undecided rather than lost; consumers of GameSummary must handle null.
Appending an entry and completing a set are two writes, so their combined failure behaviour must be defined.
revisitTriggers: Synchronised recording settles on a stable identity for entries, since replacing entry N is not a stable target once writers are concurrent, and set completion must agree with whatever anchor it chooses.
A second consumer needs a derived value stored, which should reuse this pattern rather than reintroduce per-rally accumulation.
